extracted.intended_audience: news editors, journalists, and media industry professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and processes for evaluating and managing freelance contributors in a newsroom, focusing on source verification, independent fact-checking, handling of unverifiable material, anonymous sourcing, and corrective/remedial actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent fact-checking of contributor work
rubrics_metrics.description: When sources claim they had not spoken with the writer, launch an independent investigation / fact check.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Guardian hired an independent fact checker who, after carrying out 50 interviews, found articles that contained likely or confirmed fabrication, including stories about two events that organizers said he didn’t attend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove fabricated articles and opinion pieces
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove stories found to contain fabrication from the website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In light of the extent of the fabrication and the uncertainty surrounding many of the articles, The Guardian removed 12 news stories and one opinion piece; other stories proved accurate and were left as is.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish corrections/footnotes for unverifiable content
rubrics_metrics.description: For articles that remain, remove quotes and information that could not be verified and publish explanatory notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Guardian removed unverifiable quotes/information and published footnotes on each article page to outline changes and the verification issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Due diligence on freelancers before regular assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: Know more about freelancers before they start writing regularly; perform background checks and verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are often people we haven’t met, but we go on to place an inherent degree of trust that the work they are filing to us is true. We are currently reviewing our processes in order to improve due diligence in relation to regular contributors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict enforcement and questioning of anonymous sourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: Question and more strictly enforce the use of anonymous sources; restrict anonymity to cases with a strong reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We need to take a closer look at occasions where individuals are not named in a story for no strong reason. Anonymous sourcing is necessary in some cases (e.g., sensitive national security reporting) but should not be used without strong justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require contributors to provide source information
rubrics_metrics.description: Freelancers must be able and willing to provide information on most sources cited in their reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mayton was 'unable or unwilling to provide information on most sources' — inability to supply source details is a red flag that should trigger further checks or withholding publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify existence and identity of quoted sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm that quoted sources exist and can be substantiated (not solely relying on lack of online presence or anonymous attribution).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dozens of sources could not be found — either they had no online presence or they were anonymous and could not be substantiated; organizers denied attendance at events the writer said he covered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use readers' editor / external review panels for complaints and oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Have internal and external mechanisms (readers' editor, external review panel) to handle complaints and review reporting issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Guardian is not IPSO-member in the UK context for this US-based issue, but it uses a readers’ editor and an external review panel to deal with complaints and oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public apology and assurance of improvement when errors occur
rubrics_metrics.description: Apologise publicly to those misrepresented and to readers, and commit to doing better to preserve trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Guardian apologised to people whose words were misrepresented or falsified and to readers for the errors, assuring that it will do better and improve processes.
